iteration_note: Each exam is administered annually; 10 recorded editions. Edition 1 (2017) is the canonical paper below; editions 2-10 are tracked in the version ledger as they are authored.

agents.I: State the P vs NP question precisely and define polynomial-time reductions.
agents.II: Prove that SAT is NP-complete (the Cook-Levin theorem, sketch).
agents.III: Situate the theory: Arora & Barak, Computational Complexity: A Modern Approach.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline algorithm design (field 47). Trap: must not claim P != NP is proved.

agents.I: State amortized analysis and the master theorem.
agents.II: Prove the amortized bound of a splay tree or the master-theorem recurrence solution.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Cormen, Leiserson, Rivest, Stein, Introduction to Algorithms.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline lower bounds (field 46). Trap: must not claim an amortized bound is per-operation worst case.

agents.I: Distinguish Las Vegas from Monte Carlo algorithms and state Chernoff bounds.
agents.II: Prove a Chernoff bound and analyze a randomized algorithm that uses it.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Mitzenmacher & Upfal, Probability and Computing.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline derandomization theory (field 46). Trap: must not claim a Monte Carlo algorithm's error is free.

agents.I: State the APX/PTAS landscape and gap-preserving reductions.
agents.II: Design a 2-approximation for vertex cover and prove its ratio.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Williamson & Shmoys, The Design of Approximation Algorithms.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline exact algorithms (field 47). Trap: must not claim a heuristic has a proven ratio without proof.

agents.I: Define fixed-parameter tractability and kernels.
agents.II: Prove that vertex cover is FPT and exhibit a kernel of size O(k^2).
agents.III: Situate the theory: Cygan et al., Parameterized Algorithms.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline PTAS theory (field 49). Trap: must not claim W[1]-hardness implies NP-hardness.

agents.I: State max-flow min-cut and minimum spanning tree algorithms.
agents.II: Prove the max-flow min-cut theorem (via augmenting paths or LP duality).
agents.III: Situate the theory: Cormen et al.; Schrijver, Combinatorial Optimization.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline graph theory (field 17). Trap: must not claim Dijkstra handles negative edges.

agents.I: State convex-hull algorithms and the planar point-location problem.
agents.II: Analyze Graham scan and prove its O(n log n) bound, including degeneracy handling.
agents.III: Situate the theory: de Berg et al., Computational Geometry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline rendering (field 104). Trap: must not ignore collinear or coincident degeneracies.

agents.I: State the Chomsky hierarchy and the pumping lemma.
agents.II: Prove that context-free languages are not closed under intersection.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline compiler IR (field 140). Trap: must not claim CFLs are closed under intersection.

agents.I: State the halting problem and Rice's theorem.
agents.II: Prove the undecidability of the halting problem by diagonalization.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Sipser, Introduction to the Theory of Computation.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline complexity classes (field 46). Trap: must not claim every undecidable problem reduces to halting trivially.

agents.I: Define semantic security and reductions to hard problems.
agents.II: Prove that any PRG-based stream cipher is semantically secure given the PRG assumption.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Katz & Lindell, Introduction to Modern Cryptography.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline implementation and side-channel practice (fields 150, 157). Trap: must not claim a protocol is secure without an adversary model.

agents.I: State the no-cloning theorem and distinguish superposition from entanglement.
agents.II: Prove the no-cloning theorem and derive the teleportation protocol.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Nielsen & Chuang, Quantum Computation and Quantum Information.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline quantum error correction (field 57). Trap: must not claim universal exponential speedups.

agents.I: State the Hamming bound and the role of a parity-check matrix.
agents.II: Prove the Hamming bound for binary codes and construct a Hamming code achieving it.
agents.III: Situate the theory: MacWilliams & Sloane, The Theory of Error-Correcting Codes.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline information theory (field 58). Trap: must not claim Hamming-optimal codes are optimal for all channels.

agents.I: Define entropy, mutual information, and channel capacity; state Shannon's theorem.
agents.II: Prove Shannon's noisy-channel coding theorem (achievability for the DMC).
agents.III: Situate the theory: Cover & Thomas, Elements of Information Theory.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline code constructions (field 57). Trap: must not claim capacity is achieved by short codes.

agents.I: Define the price of anarchy and Nash equilibrium in routing games.
agents.II: Prove the price of anarchy bound for selfish routing on affine latencies.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Nisan et al., Algorithmic Game Theory.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline mechanism design (field 387). Trap: must not claim pure-strategy Nash always exists.

agents.I: State total unimodularity and its consequence for integral polytopes.
agents.II: Prove that the LP relaxation of a network-flow problem with totally unimodular matrix is integral.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Schrijver, Combinatorial Optimization.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline IP solver internals (field 22). Trap: must not claim LP relaxations of ILPs are always integral.

agents.I: Define epsilon-testers and the proximity-oblivious model.
agents.II: Construct a tester for bipartiteness with bounded queries and prove its guarantees.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Goldreich, Introduction to Property Testing.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline streaming algorithms (field 166). Trap: must not claim passing a tester certifies the property.

agents.I: Define the competitive ratio and the ski-rental problem.
agents.II: Prove that the optimal deterministic ski-rental algorithm has competitive ratio 2.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Borodin & El-Yaniv, Online Computation and Competitive Analysis.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline stochastic optimization (field 79). Trap: must not claim average-case behavior implies competitiveness.

agents.I: State universal approximation and its limits; the depth-width trade-off.
agents.II: Prove the universal approximation theorem for a single hidden layer (sketch via Fourier/Stone-Weierstrass).
agents.III: Situate the theory: Goodfellow, Bengio, Courville, Deep Learning.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline architecture engineering (field 64). Trap: must not claim universal approximation implies learnability.

agents.I: Explain scaled dot-product attention and the 1/sqrt(d) factor.
agents.II: Derive the complexity of self-attention and state what FlashAttention changes.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Vaswani et al., Attention Is All You Need (2017).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline fine-tuning practice (field 119). Trap: must not claim attention is inherently interpretable.

agents.I: State the GAN min-max objective and the mode collapse problem.
agents.II: Derive the optimal discriminator for a fixed generator and the resulting Jensen-Shannon objective.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Goodfellow et al. 2014; Kingma & Welling 2013.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline diffusion math (field 66). Trap: must not claim GAN training provably converges.

agents.I: State the forward and reverse diffusion processes and the denoising ELBO.
agents.II: Derive the DDPM training objective from the variational lower bound on the reverse process.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Ho et al. 2020 (DDPM); Sohl-Dickstein et al. 2015.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline GANs (field 65). Trap: must not claim sampling needs the true score.

agents.I: State the Bellman optimality equation and exploration vs exploitation.
agents.II: Prove the convergence of Q-learning for finite MDPs with a tabular representation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Sutton & Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline control theory (field 124). Trap: must not claim Q-learning converges with arbitrary function approximation.

agents.I: State the non-stationarity problem and MARL equilibrium concepts.
agents.II: Prove that independent Q-learners need not converge to a Nash equilibrium (counterexample).
agents.III: Situate the theory: Busoniu et al. 2008; Yang & Wang 2020 survey.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline single-agent RL (field 67). Trap: must not claim independent learners converge to Nash.

agents.I: State behavioral cloning's compounding error and what IRL recovers.
agents.II: Prove that behavioral cloning has quadratic compounding error under distribution shift.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Ross et al. 2011 (DAgger); Abbeel & Ng 2004.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline policy gradients (field 67). Trap: must not assume demonstrations are optimal.

agents.I: State maximum likelihood vs MAP and the notion of calibration.
agents.II: Derive the MAP estimate as regularized MLE and compute the posterior for a Gaussian likelihood.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Murphy, Probabilistic Machine Learning.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline Bayesian theory (field 34). Trap: must not claim softmax outputs are calibrated probabilities.

agents.I: State d-separation and the complexity of exact inference (treewidth).
agents.II: Prove the independence semantics of d-separation for Bayesian networks.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Koller & Friedman, Probabilistic Graphical Models.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline Bayesian statistics (field 34). Trap: must not claim loopy belief propagation always converges.

agents.I: State the kernel's role and the posterior predictive; expected improvement.
agents.II: Derive the GP posterior predictive distribution from the joint Gaussian assumption.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rasmussen & Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline kernel RKHS theory (field 73). Trap: must not claim GP inference is cheap (O(n^3)).

agents.I: State the representer theorem and the kernel trick.
agents.II: Prove the representer theorem and derive the SVM dual.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Scholkopf & Smola, Learning with Kernels.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline deep learning (field 63). Trap: must not claim universal kernels make anything learnable in finite samples.

agents.I: State the bias-variance decomposition of bagging and boosting.
agents.II: Derive the bias-variance decomposition of the squared error and apply it to bagging.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hastie et al., The Elements of Statistical Learning.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline deep ensembles (field 80). Trap: must not claim more trees always help.

agents.I: State the InfoNCE objective and triplet losses.
agents.II: Derive the InfoNCE bound relating the contrastive loss to mutual information.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Chen et al. 2020 (SimCLR); Hadsell et al. 2006.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline retrieval systems (field 86). Trap: must not claim cosine similarity equals semantic similarity.

agents.I: State pretext tasks vs contrastive objectives and representation collapse.
agents.II: Prove that a trivial constant representation minimizes the standard contrastive loss and explain the prevention.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Liu et al. 2021 survey; Chen et al. 2020.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline downstream benchmarking (field 120). Trap: must not claim SSL features work for every downstream task.

agents.I: State MAML's bi-level objective and catastrophic forgetting.
agents.II: Derive the MAML update as a bi-level optimization and its first-order approximation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Finn et al. 2017 (MAML).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline continual learning (field 79). Trap: must not claim meta-learning generalizes to unseen task distributions.

agents.I: State FedAvg and the non-IID data problem.
agents.II: Prove the convergence bound for FedAvg under bounded-gradient and smoothness assumptions (sketch).
agents.III: Situate the theory: McMahan et al. 2017.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline privacy proofs (field 159). Trap: must not claim FL provides differential privacy by default.

agents.I: State the stability-plasticity dilemma and replay methods.
agents.II: Prove the lower bound on forgetting for a simple two-task continual learning problem.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Parisi et al. 2019 survey.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline meta-learning (field 77). Trap: must not claim EWC fully prevents forgetting.

agents.I: State the temperature role in knowledge distillation.
agents.II: Derive the softened KL objective of distillation and its gradient in the high-temperature limit.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hinton et al. 2015.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline hardware deployment (field 482). Trap: must not claim pruning preserves accuracy without fine-tuning.

agents.I: State SHAP's Shapley-value basis and its axioms.
agents.II: Prove that Shapley values are the unique attribution satisfying the four axioms (efficiency, symmetry, dummy, additivity).
agents.III: Situate the theory: Lundberg & Lee 2017; Ribeiro et al. 2016 (LIME).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline causal inference (field 83). Trap: must not claim feature attribution equals causation.

agents.I: State the adversarial-example phenomenon and the PGD training objective.
agents.II: Prove the existence of adversarial examples for a linear classifier under the Linf budget.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Madry et al. 2018; Goodfellow et al. 2015 (FGSM).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline security deployment (field 160). Trap: must not claim certified robustness is free.

agents.I: State do-calculus and the identification of causal effects; define confounding.
agents.II: Prove the back-door adjustment formula and the conditions under which it identifies the effect.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Pearl, Causality; Hernan & Robins.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline prediction (field 70). Trap: must not claim ML automatically adjusts confounders.

agents.I: State the forecasting hierarchy and the role of backtesting.
agents.II: Derive the optimal one-step predictor for an ARIMA model from its state-space form.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hyndman & Athanasopoulos, Forecasting: Principles and Practice.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline ARIMA diagnostics (field 36). Trap: must not claim ML beats statistical baselines without proper evaluation.

agents.I: State the class-imbalance problem and reconstruction-based methods.
agents.II: Derive the anomaly score of a Gaussian autoencoder and its decision boundary.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Chandola et al. 2009 survey.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline IDS deployment (field 155). Trap: must not claim unsupervised detection yields calibrated probabilities.

agents.I: State collaborative filtering vs content-based methods and the cold-start problem.
agents.II: Derive the matrix-factorization objective and its alternating least squares solution.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Ricci et al., Recommender Systems Handbook.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline IR ranking (field 173). Trap: must not claim offline metrics predict online engagement.

agents.I: State message passing and its expressivity limits (Weisfeiler-Lehman).
agents.II: Prove that GIN is as expressive as the 1-WL test for distinguishing graphs.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kipf & Welling 2017 (GCN); Xu et al. 2019 (GIN).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline graph algorithms (field 51). Trap: must not claim GNNs generalize across graph sizes.

agents.I: State the search space / strategy / estimation loop and weight sharing.
agents.II: Derive the DARTS continuous relaxation and its bilevel objective.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Elsken et al. 2019 survey.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline hyperparameter tuning (field 72). Trap: must not claim NAS results are Pareto-optimal without cost analysis.

agents.I: State uncertainty sampling vs query-by-committee.
agents.II: Prove the generalization benefit of uncertainty sampling for a threshold classifier (under assumptions).
agents.III: Situate the theory: Settles, Active Learning survey.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline Bayesian optimization (field 72). Trap: must not claim active learning always beats random sampling.

agents.I: State Adam's bias correction and the role of the loss landscape.
agents.II: Derive the Adam update with bias correction from the EMA of gradients and squared gradients.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kingma & Ba 2015; Loshchilov & Hutter (AdamW).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline convex optimization (field 22). Trap: must not claim Adam always converges best.

agents.I: State the AlexNet-to-ResNet evolution and the role of data augmentation.
agents.II: Derive the residual learning formulation and explain why skip connections ease optimization.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Krizhevsky et al. 2012; He et al. 2016 (ResNet).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline detection (field 92). Trap: must not claim ImageNet accuracy transfers to every domain.

agents.I: State anchor-based vs anchor-free detectors and the roles of IoU and NMS.
agents.II: Derive the Faster R-CNN two-stage objective and the RoI pooling operation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Ren et al. 2015; He et al. 2017 (Mask R-CNN).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline classification (field 91). Trap: must not claim mAP reflects deployment robustness.

agents.I: State temporal modeling (3D convolutions vs transformers).
agents.II: Derive the I3D architecture from 2D convolutions via inflation and justify its parameter efficiency.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Carreira & Zisserman 2017 (I3D).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline tracking (field 103). Trap: must not claim video models are frame-rate invariant.

agents.I: State epipolar geometry and the SfM vs SLAM distinction.
agents.II: Derive the essential matrix constraint and the eight-point algorithm.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Hartley & Zisserman, Multiple View Geometry.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline neural rendering (field 95). Trap: must not claim metric scale without calibration.

agents.I: State the NeRF volumetric rendering equation.
agents.II: Derive the volume-rendering integral from transmittance and density, and the stratified sampling estimator.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Mildenhall et al. 2020 (NeRF).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline rasterization (field 104). Trap: must not claim NeRF generalizes to arbitrary unseen views.

agents.I: State text-to-image conditioning and inversion-based editing.
agents.II: Derive DDIM inversion and explain why it enables editing in latent space.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Rombach et al. 2022 (Stable Diffusion); Hertz et al. 2022.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline diffusion theory (field 66). Trap: must not claim generated images are factual or rights-clear.

agents.I: State contrastive visual pretraining and linear-probe evaluation.
agents.II: Derive the MoCo momentum-updated dictionary and why it stabilizes contrastive learning.
agents.III: Situate the theory: He et al. 2020 (MoCo); Chen et al. 2020 (SimCLR).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline supervised classification (field 91). Trap: must not claim features are domain-agnostic.

agents.I: State ArcFace embeddings and the template-matching protocol; define spoofing.
agents.II: Derive the ArcFace additive angular margin loss and its effect on the decision boundary.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Deng et al. 2019 (ArcFace).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline privacy law (field 437). Trap: must not claim accuracy generalizes across demographics.

agents.I: State the annotation problem and domain shift across scanners.
agents.II: Derive a U-Net's downsampling/upsampling path and its memory-IO trade-off for segmentation.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Litjens et al. 2017 survey; Ronneberger et al. 2015.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline clinical diagnosis (field 327). Trap: must not claim a model is clinically validated without a trial.

agents.I: State multispectral processing and cloud masking.
agents.II: Derive the NDVI index and analyze its sensitivity to atmospheric path radiance.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Richards & Jia, Remote Sensing Digital Image Analysis.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline climate science (field 355). Trap: must not claim sub-pixel accuracy without ground truth.

agents.I: State HDR merging and demosaicing.
agents.II: Derive the burst-photography pipeline: registration, denoising, and merging as a single optimization.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Szeliski, Computer Vision; Hasinoff et al. 2016.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline optics (field 224). Trap: must not claim HDR removes motion blur.

agents.I: State panoptic segmentation and scene graphs.
agents.II: Derive the panoptic quality metric and its decomposition into segmentation and recognition terms.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Kirillov et al. 2019; Johnson et al. 2015.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline detection primitives (field 92). Trap: must not claim scene graphs capture all relations.

agents.I: State Siamese trackers and association (Hungarian).
agents.II: Derive the DeepSORT cascade matching and the appearance-motion fusion metric.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Bertinetto et al. 2016 (SiamFC); Bewley et al. 2016 (DeepSORT).
agents.IV: Scope: must decline detection (field 92). Trap: must not claim a tracker is occlusion-proof.

agents.I: State rasterization vs ray tracing and define a BRDF.
agents.II: Derive the rendering equation and the path-tracing estimator of the outgoing radiance.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Pharr et al., Physically Based Rendering.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline neural rendering (field 95). Trap: must not claim real-time ray tracing equals offline quality.

agents.I: State Bezier/B-spline theory and skinning.
agents.II: Derive the de Casteljau algorithm and prove the affine-invariance of Bezier curves.
agents.III: Situate the theory: Farin, Curves and Surfaces for CAGD.
agents.IV: Scope: must decline simulation physics (field 489). Trap: must not claim subdivision surfaces are C-infinity everywhere.
